Dengue Test Guide: NS1, IgM & IgG - Which One Do You Need?

Fever, severe body pain, headache, or weakness during mosquito season may seem like a common viral illness, but these could be signs of dengue that should not be ignored. Understanding the dengue test guide: NS1, IgM & IgG, can help you know when and which test is required.

The NS1 dengue test is usually recommended during the early stage of infection, typically within the first 1-5 days of fever. It helps detect the dengue virus quickly during the active phase of infection.

The IgM dengue test is generally advised after 5 days of symptoms, as it helps identify a recent dengue infection by detecting antibodies produced by the body.

The IgG dengue test is used to check for past dengue infection or secondary dengue exposure. It helps doctors understand whether the infection is current or from a previous exposure.
Choosing the right dengue test at the right time is important for proper diagnosis and medical care. Delaying testing may increase the risk of complications, especially if symptoms like persistent fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, or weakness worsen.

A Rheumatoid Arthritis test helps detect autoimmune activity in the body where the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy joints. Blood tests such as Rheumatoid Factor (RF), Anti-CCP antibodies, and inflammatory markers like ESR and CRP play a key role in identifying this condition early.

What is a Bone Marrow Test?

Unexplained fatigue, frequent infections, or unusual bruising may seem like minor concerns, but they could be signs of underlying blood-related conditions that require deeper investigation.
A bone marrow test is a diagnostic procedure used to examine the soft tissue inside your bones where blood cells are produced. This test helps doctors evaluate the production of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, and is often recommended to diagnose or monitor conditions like anaemia, infections, blood disorders, or certain cancers.

When routine blood tests show abnormal results, a bone marrow test provides more detailed information about what is happening inside your body. It can help identify the cause of low blood counts, detect infections, or assess diseases affecting the bone marrow.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr Viraj Sadrani, besides managing his patholab is also empanelled with Star Yellow Fever Vaccination centre Mira Road for administrating yellow fever vaccination in private by charging a premium fee.
I am narrating my harrowing experience with him yesterday regarding my yellow fever vaccination appointment for three of us - my husband, my 5 YO son and for myself.
Never in my life have I met an arrogant, impolite, vainglorious human being as Viraj Sadrani.
Let me give you a background. Cost of a yellow fever vaccine in any Govt establishment is Rs.300 per dose, however I paid Rs. 2500 per dose - that's Rs 7500 for the three of us- more than 8 times the actual price!  When you pay a premium , you expect a service complimenting that - forget about service , this guy walked in  1 and a half hour late and with zero remorse. Now remember that we also had my 5 YO with us - imagine the trauma he would have been in for 1 and a half hour that he waited for his shot to be administered!
Forget about sorry  - my husband's one statement that Dr we had to wait too long for you , triggered his self centred ego so much that he started raising his voice on us - we kept on saying try to understand our point of view as well , but this guys was so full of himself that he finally said - you may choose to walk out without the vaccination - stop shouting here! When I interjected and said I am not the one shouting here, you are ; like am immature kid, he dragged his assistant into this conversation and started asking- tu bata koun chilla raha hai ! Imagine the level of immaturity and unprofessionalism he has!
Not just this , he also threw his weight around citing twice that he was a DOCTOR! As if we were some uneducated goons sitting infront of him! This entire experience was so disturbing for all three of us specially  for my child that he broke into tears towards the end!

All we needed was a simple 'Sorry' but that would have meant stooping too low for this egoist person- forget about him apologising, I had to apologise to him at the end to ease out the tension there!

Think twice before reaching out to this unprofessional doctor in future- remember he is not the last doctor remaining on this Earth- there is no dearth of Doctors  !

It's high time doctors started treating us as their customers and not as mere patients in dire need of them . We pay for their services and they better learn punctuality and professionalism.
